newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rates stable, trade slow.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rates stable, trade slow.

text.p: Croatian money market trade was slow on Thursday thanks to replenished bank accounts, dealers said.
"We have seen relatively little trade today due to the banks not being in search of funds," a dealer told Reuters.
She said some banks even asked to repay loans before due date because of their good liquidity.
Fresh borrowings totalled 19.9 million kuna, most of which were call money loans struck at an unchanged 10.5 percent.
One 30-day interbank deal was made at a regular 15 percent and savings banks were granted one-month funds at 15 and 16 percent.
Some 25 million kuna has been left on the supply side.
Monday's overnight trade totalled 5 million kuna borrowed by one bank to maintain its mandatory reserve. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
